title: Understanding numbers
content: Numbers are symbols used for counting and measuring. Examples include 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5.

title: Introduction to addition
content: Addition means combining numbers to find their total. For example 2 plus 3 equals 5.

title: Addition using objects
content: To calculate 3 plus 2 place three objects in one group and two objects in another group. Count all the objects to get 5.

title: Introduction to subtraction
content: Subtraction means taking one quantity away from another. For example 5 minus 2 equals 3.

title: Introduction to multiplication
content: Multiplication is repeated addition. Three multiplied by four means adding four three times: 4 plus 4 plus 4 equals 12.

title: Multiplication using groups
content: Four groups of two objects contain eight objects altogether. Therefore 4 multiplied by 2 equals 8.

title: Introduction to division
content: Division means sharing a quantity equally or arranging it into equal groups. Twelve divided by three equals four.

title: Introduction to fractions
content: A fraction represents part of a whole. In one half the number 1 is the numerator and 2 is the denominator.

title: Equivalent fractions
content: Equivalent fractions have the same value even though they use different numbers. One half and two quarters represent the same amount.

title: Introduction to decimals
content: Decimals represent whole numbers and parts of a whole. In 2.5 the digit 2 represents two wholes and 5 represents five tenths.

title: Area of a rectangle
content: Area is the amount of space inside a shape. The area of a rectangle is calculated by multiplying its length by its width.

title: Perimeter of a rectangle
content: Perimeter is the total distance around a shape. Add the lengths of all the sides to find the perimeter.

title: Introduction to percentages
content: A percentage describes a quantity out of one hundred. Fifty percent means fifty out of one hundred.

title: Introduction to ratios
content: A ratio compares two or more quantities. A ratio of two red balls to three blue balls is written as 2 to 3.

title: Understanding triangles
content: A triangle is a closed two-dimensional shape with three straight sides and three angles.
